The investigation has also revealed that the group has up to 198 affiliated companies, with 98 located in Cambodia and another 100 spread overseas. Additionally, a key member of the Prince Group, Ing Dara, has been arrested in Cambodia and is being processed by the court. bonuses.requirements: Anthropic's IPO Filing Reveals Net Loss Expanded to $80.7 Billion in First HalfHomeFeedNewsAnthropic's IPO Filing Reveals Net Loss Expanded to $80.7 Billion in First HalfAnthropic's IPO Filing Reveals Net Loss Expanded to $80.7 Billion in First Half10/22 09:00Artificial intelligence company Anthropic is gearing up for its IPO. The draft prospectus shows that revenue for the first half of 2026 increased to $16.3 billion from $1.1 billion in the same period last year, while net loss widened from $13 billion to $80.7 billion. Of this, $72 billion is attributed to the accounting revaluation of financing instruments such as convertible notes, where the increase in valuation makes the conversion rights more valuable. The fair value increase of related financing liabilities must be recognized as a loss in the income statement, although it does not represent an equivalent cash outflow in the current period; however, future conversions may dilute existing shareholders. The total net loss for the previous year was $42 billion, of which approximately $34 billion stemmed from similar accounting adjustments. In the first half, investments in computing power and infrastructure reached nearly $9 billion, compared to $2.3 billion in the same period last year. bonuses.requirements: Kuala Lumpur Court Orders Return of 497.82 BitcoinsHomeFeedNewsKuala Lumpur Court Orders Return of 497.82 BitcoinsKuala Lumpur Court Orders Return of 497.82 Bitcoins10/22 09:00According to Malaysian media reports, the Kuala Lumpur High Court has ruled that the government must return a total of 497.82 bitcoins to nine victims of an investment scam. Based on 2023 valuations, this batch of bitcoins is worth approximately 17.6 million USD. The court found that between 2015 and 2016, the nine victims were deceived by Fadino Khairuman and Asyran Ismail, who convinced them to deposit a total of 362.04 bitcoins into a Bitkingdom wallet, promising a daily investment return of 1%. The relevant bitcoins were subsequently transferred to wallets under the names of the two individuals and were eventually seized by law enforcement. The judge noted that the bitcoins involved underwent multiple transactions and transfers, indicating a layered processing of funds; however, the victims did not lend bitcoins to the defendants but lost their assets due to fraud, thus holding legitimate rights to the seized assets. The court ruled that the 497.82 bitcoins should be distributed according to the proportion of each victim's initial investment, with each person receiving between 0.68% to 11.7% of the total.BullishBearishLikeShareDisclaimer：The content above does not represent HTX's positions.，HTX does not provide any trading recommendations.。Related ArticlesBitcoin Whales Accumulate 88,987 BTC, Why Are Traders Still Cautious?Bitcoin price dips below $82K as high oil prices spike US CPI inflationBTC price support holds ahead of US CPI data: Three things Bitcoin traders need to know this weekAll Comments0LatestHotLatestHotTrending TopicsRelated ArticlesBitcoin Whales Accumulate 88,987 BTC, Why Are Traders Still Cautious?Bitcoin price dips below $82K as high oil prices spike US CPI inflationBTC price support holds ahead of US CPI data: Three things Bitcoin traders need to know this week

Huang Renxun 'Puts Out Fire': Financing Costs Declining, No Need for NVIDIA to Provide BackstopmarsbitPublished on 2026-10-16Last updated on 2026-10-16AbstractCoreWeave, a major AI cloud service provider and key NVIDIA customer, is facing heightened credit market concerns. Its five-year credit default swap (CDS) spreads soared to a record high of over 1190 basis points, implying a perceived default probability exceeding 60%. Concurrently, its bond prices plummeted, with yields surging above 15-16%, reflecting intense investor worries about its ability to service nearly $50 billion in debt while remaining unprofitable.

This stress is spreading within the AI infrastructure sector. CDS spreads for companies like Oracle, SoftBank, NVIDIA, and others also widened significantly, indicating a broader market reassessment of the debt risks behind massive AI capital expenditures.

In response, NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang publicly expressed confidence in CoreWeave, stating its "financial strength is growing daily" and its cost of capital is declining. He explicitly stated NVIDIA sees no need to provide a financial backstop for CoreWeave, in which it holds a roughly 10% stake. His comments helped CoreWeave's stock recover from early losses.

The core issue under scrutiny is whether the future cash flows from AI investments can cover the enormous upfront costs and interest burdens, especially as financing becomes more expensive. The situation highlights a critical shift in market focus: from purely evaluating AI compute demand to questioning the sustainability of the debt-fueled expansion models used to build that capacity.#AI Infrastructure#Bond Yield#CDS#Cloud Computing#CoreWeave#Credit Markets#Debt#Default Risk#Financing#Jensen Huang
